context: Decide where permanence attaches - at commit, as documented, or at publication - and make the written contract match the minted value either way. An alias mechanism is only worth building if permanence attaches before the corpus stops moving.
description: hosted-results-contract.md records public_result_id as permanent once minted, with format {benchmark}-{platform}-sf{scale_factor}-{date} and collisions resolved by the minting service appending -{n}. What is actually minted carries a content-hash suffix, so the documented format and the documented collision mechanism are both wrong, and every re-derivation of the corpus changes every id. #1537 rotates all 207. There is no alias or redirect mechanism, and no deployed Explorer, so the cost is zero today and non-zero after the first public deploy. This follows the field-set decision because that decision determines whether another rotation is coming.

preserves.behavior: Ids stay content-addressed unless the ADR deliberately trades that away and says what replaces it
Whatever is decided must hold before the Explorer's first public deploy

verifications.description: the documented format names the content-hash suffix that is actually minted
